title: Minimax Estimation of Hellinger Distance between Potential Categorical Outcome Distributions
banked_reason: Sound all-design original-record categorical Hellinger minimax frontier; D0.5.G paper_score_ceiling 6.9 < 7.4, tier subfield below required field, NOT salvageable in scope. Independent D and main validity gates confirm below-floor stop.
gap_reasons: The delivered proofs establish the universal-factor minimax risk, the J=o(n) consistency criterion, and exact risk 1/4 for J≥2n against the stipulated unrestricted competitors. They do not determine exact risk below saturation or exact optimality of fair assignment; linear-alphabet-value remains open, and the framing does not present it as settled.

The practical precision claim exceeds the demonstrated operational evidence: the certified procedure always returns 1/2 for n≤1256, and the large upper constants leave substantial uncertainty about useful finite-cohort performance.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the full-table all-design rate Θ(min{1,1/n+J²/n²}), uniform consistency iff J=o(n), and exact risk 1/4 for J≥2n, with a total finite-arithmetic fair-assignment procedure and original-record converses. Typed math review and independent D/main validity audits found the kernel sound; the completed package remained subfield at score ceiling 6.9 below the standing field threshold 7.4, with no bounded tier lift. Exact critical-regime value/design, sharper useful finite-cohort guarantees, and a delivered application remain future work; no Lean formalization, F phase, promotion, presentation or git commit was performed.
tldr: A randomized experiment measures a distributional contrast of the actual enrolled cohort. The target \(\theta_H\) is the squared Hellinger distance between two complete empirical categorical margins, already defined in the causal literature. The focal object \(R_H(n,J)\) jointly optimizes every ex ante design and every total full-record rule. Integer-count root inversion, explicit coupling-error control, and posterior uncertainty of the realized target supply finite risk certificates. The main question evaluates the universal-factor frontier and its exact consistency criterion, including sparse cells and saturation. A separate question exposes the genuinely unresolved exact risk in the linear-alphabet regime. The intended consumer is a prospective earnings or income trial with one fixed follow-up and predeclared bins.
gap: Independent-sample population divergence estimation and scalar finite-cohort experimental minimax theory leave the paired empirical categorical affinity experiment unevaluated. Their likelihoods and target-preserving reductions differ from this experiment.
fill: Root-count observation-operator inversion and full-table posterior certificates address the complete \(n,J\) problem. An observable finite-arithmetic rule supplies attainment, while identical labeled-record laws and missing-bit fluctuations supply all-design necessity. The sharper critical-regime question records the remaining constant-level content.
